chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

You wipe with your right hand upon your forehead and your face at the end of Al-Maghrib prayer and the other prayers, and you say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Knower of the Hidden and the Apparent, the Beneficent, the Merciful, Who there is no god except Him. O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from worry, grief, sickness, deficiency, lowliness, disgrace, and immoralities, whatever is apparent of them and whatever is hidden.'

key_terms.عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَ الشَّهَادَةِ: The Knower of the Hidden and the Apparent

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and action after Maghrib prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the specific act of masah (wiping) on the forehead and face with the right hand after Maghrib and other prayers, a practice central to Shia ritual jurisprudence. The accompanying supplication invokes Allah’s attributes as the Knower of the unseen and seen, seeking refuge from both manifest and hidden afflictions, thereby linking physical ritual with spiritual protection.
